reading.body:
DartPoints Baton Rouge 2 publishes 3 MW of IT capacity, making it the only facility in Louisiana with a disclosed megawatt figure, though three other mapped sites in the state do not publish capacity data.

At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 3 MW supports roughly 75 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a more typical enterprise density, it supports roughly 300 racks. These are assumptions about rack density, not operator claims. No redundancy tier, power usage effectiveness figure, or cooling architecture is published, so no further inference about uptime class or thermal headroom is warranted.

Three megawatts is a small footprint by the standards of campuses built to serve large-scale AI training, which routinely run into tens or hundreds of megawatts. Whether this site is relevant to AI workloads depends on use cases such as inference at the edge or regional network aggregation that do not require dense GPU clusters. That determination requires tenant and workload data that is not published.

Certifications are not published in the specification data provided, so no statement about what compliance regimes this campus satisfies can be made.
